seal.statement: Per-node serve eligibility is one fact with one owner: the control-plane readiness owner answers it from a committed read of the nodes rows (status, boot incarnation, ready lease) and the latest published control_plane_publications row (publication epoch, published active nodes, priority spread) taken on the raft leaders of those system partitions, as {decision, epoch} or a typed UNAVAILABLE{reason, epoch, retryAfterMs}; the readiness snapshot is a memo keyed by that epoch and a stale memo answers UNAVAILABLE_STALE{epoch}. User-table routing, CREATE TABLE provisioning (complete at the sealed quorum minimum with a typed under_replicated outcome naming the epoch and missing count, or PROVISIONING_UNAVAILABLE mapped to SQLSTATE 57P03), the rebalancer's critical-topology settle, available-node and local-serve decisions, the in-flight operations source and the learner count check consume that answer or the committed lease it is built from. System-table routing decides on raft leadership and live transport, never on serve eligibility, so no readiness carve-out is needed. Deleted: the system-table leader fail-open and its inline evidence-absent set, readiness-denial-classification.js, the priority-recovery bootstrap routing bypass and its read lane, the fresh-bootstrap routing grace, every !== false and empty-means-satisfied default on a readiness input, allowStaleOnCacheChange and maxCachedAgeMs on decision paths, the degraded provisioning fallback, the provisioning convergence poll and its 10 s constant, the transient-shortfall minimum lowering, and the CACHE source of in-flight topology operations. On a fresh three-node formation the serve lane opens on every node.
